The man in a fright tried to utter the spell given under No. 1444, but lost his head and broke down at the second word. 2168. అర్థము "లేనివాడు నిరర్థకుడు. A man without money is useless. (See No. 1876.) A man without money is like a ship without sails, (Dud. \ 2169. అర్ధము "లేనివాడు వ్యర్థుడు. A man without money is vain. 2170. అల్లికాయల సందడిని పెండ్లి మరిచినాడు. In his haste about the Alli kayas he forgot the marriage. Alli kaya is the fruit of the Memecylon Capitellatum. 2171. అవ్వా గుర్రమూ వకటి అయినట్టు. The grandmother and the horse were one. A man and his grandmother started on a journey, the former riding, the latter on foot; the grandson rested frequently on the road and eventaally only reached his destination just as his grandmother had completed her journey. The tortoise and the hare. 2172. అశ్వత్ధ ప్రదమీణము GR, కడుపు పట్టి చూచుకొన్నదట. While she was going round the holy fig tree, she felt for signs of pregnancy. Expecting the result to be obtained at the very commencement of an enterprize. * Een man sonder geld is een schip zonder seflen. (6 )

pages.text: TELUGU PROVERBS—SUPPLEMENT. అ. 2173. అకలి కాకుండా నీకు జెషధము యిస్తాను నీ యింట్లో చద్ది నాకు "పెట్టు అన్నాడట. I'll give you medicine to keep away hunger, give me your cold breakfast. Said by a quack. 2174. అకలికొన్నవాడు యొంగిటికి యేవగించడు. The hungry man will not refuse leavings. 2175. ఆకాశం గద్ద తన్నుకొని పోయినది. The sky was kicked away by the kite. Said in answer to an impertinent question. 2116, ఆకాశానికి నిచ్చెన వేశేవాడు. A man who plants a ladder on the sky. Ambitious. 2177. ఆచారం ముందర, అనావారం వెనక. Purity first and impurity after. Impurity always attends purity. 2178. అచార్యునికి ద్రోహము చేశినా, ఆత్మకు ద్రోహం చెయ్యరాదు. Though you cheat your priest you should not cheat your own life. Take good care of yourself, even thongh you treat your priest badly. Said by a selfish, greedy man. (7)

pages.text: ఆం ధ్రృలోకో కిచ 0ద్ర,కా శేషము. 2179. ఆడదాని బుధ్ధి అపర బుద్ధి. A woman’s sense is wrong sense. (See No. 438.) Lit. in the back of the head. 2180. ఆడపిల్లను కన్నవారు అయిదు బిరుదులు అెగకోసుకోవలెను. They who beget female children must cut off five of their badges of honor. A man though raised to a distinguished position in the world has yet to humble himself before his sons-in-law for the sake of his daughters, who might otherwise not be well treated. 2181. అడే కాలూ పాడే నూరూ వూరకుండవు. A dancing foot and a singing mouth are never quiet. (Bee Nos. 255, 1085, 1689. ) 2182. ఆత్మకు ద్రోహం చేస్తే అప్పుడే అడుగుతుంది. If you cheat your life, it will then and there ask [ for food ]. 2183. అఆ మంట యీ మంట, ట్రాహ్మణార్థం కడుపు మంట. [ Talk of] that burning and this burning, this Brahmanfrtha is belly burning. Said by a greedy Vaidika Brahman. Brahmanartha is an invitation issued to two or three Brahmans on the anniversary of the death of a relative. 2184. అవమూట అనివీింతామూా మామగారా. Shall we have that word said? O father-in-law! When a Kémati was dying and the word ‘‘ Nérféyana’’ had to be pro- nounced in his ears, all his relations tried to shirk this disagreeable duty. The allusion in the proverb is to a proposal made by one of them that the task should be imposed upon the oldest man present. 2185. ఆముదపు విత్తులు, అణి ముత్యాలు అననా. Will castor oil seeds become fine pearls ? (8)

pages.text: TELUGU PROVERBS—SUPPLEMENT. 2186. ఆయన వుంశే, విస్తరి అయినా కుట్టును. If he were here, he would at least stitch the leaf platter. (See No, 46.) 2187. ఆరంభ BK wo. Valour in the beginning. Dash, but not steady unflinching courage. 2188. అర్భాటానకు ఆరు కుంపట్లు వక్ దుంపదాలి. Six chafing dishes and a fire of roots were the cause of the uproar. 2౨189. ఆలు గుణవంతురాలు అయిళతే, మేలు కలుగును. If the wife is of good disposition, good will accrue. 2190. అళ్లు కొత్తవి అయితే, తిరగండ్లు కొత్తవా. Though the Allu be new, are the mill stones new ? ( For dns eee No. 82. ) An answer to a lame excuse. 2191, SSAow OF wo గుమ్మడి కాయ గుల్లకాసుగా యెొంచేవాడు. A man who saves a mustard seed and thinks a pumpkin worth a shell-coin. ( For Gummadi kaya see No. 517. ) Penny wise and pound foolish. They drink their water by measure, but eat their cake without. (Greek.)* 2192. ఆవుల సాధుత్వమూ, DySyewo పవేదరికమూ లేదు. There is no meekness in cows, nor poverty in Brahmans. * Mézem cdwp mlvovres auérpas pilav edovres. 2 (9)

pages.text: ఆ౦ధ్రలో కోక్సి చం ద్ర, కా శేషము. 2103. ఆళ అలి మాద, ఆధారం Wes మోద. His desire is on his wife and his support on his mat. Nothing for it but resignation. 2194. ఆశలేనివానికి చేశ మెందుకు. Why should a man without desire be in the world ? త్త. 2195. ఇంటి విల్లికి పొరుగింటి పిల్లి తోడు. The neighbour’s cat is the ally of the house cat. Both join in mischief. 2196. ఇచ్చకాలవారు బుచ్చకాలవారు పొట్ట కొరకు పొక్కులు గోకుతారు. Sycophants scratch pimples for a livelihood. 219౧ ఇచ్చేటప్పుడు కాముని పండగ, పుచ్చుకొనేటప్పుడు దీపావళి పండగ, Giving is like Kama’s festival, taking is like the feast of Dipavali. Kamadakana is the mournful commemoration of the burning of Kandarpa or Kamadeva ( the god of love) by the fire from Siva’s eye, when he in- terrupted the god in his devotions. Dipavali or Dipali is a joyous festival with nocturnal illuminations in honour of Kartikeya. The name signifies ‘a row of lamps.” 2198. ఇత్యపులు కూయగా కోనంగుడేయగా ! అవ్యేక దంతుండు పున్న పుంసకమెక్కి ఆడెనన్తూ॥ When the Ityapis cried, and Konanga shot [his darts, J Apyekadanta mounted the Punnapumsakam and danced O lady! An absurd couplet composed by a would-be poet. He attempted to make use of the synonyms given in the Amara Kosha; in his ignorance he mistook Jtyapi( ‘so also’) fora name ef the cuckoo, divided the words Darpakonanga (names of Ka&madeva) wrongly, taking Konanga, used Apyckadanta (‘also Ekadanta”’ ) as a name of Ganeéa and read Punnapumsakam (‘masculine and neuter’) as a synonym of Palmika (‘tan anthill."" )—( See Colebrooke’s Amura Kosha 2nd edn., pp. 5,7, 76,1381.) (10)

pages.text: TELUGU PROVERBS—SUPPLEMENT. 2199. ఇరుగింటమా పారుగింటమ్థా మా యింటిఆయన గోడు చూడండి. O lady neighbours! see the conduct of my husband. Invitiug the sympathy of those who cannot interfere. 2200. ఇరుసుకు కంబెన పెట్టక, పరమేశ్వరుని బండి అయినా పారదు.
